utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good morning to you. I ask you to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you are receiving interpretation of what I'm saying in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, please take your chair. Appearances, Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Ann Sutherland, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner and good morning to you. When I say to you it means the three of you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is John Ackerman, I'm with David Cunningham and Aleksandar Vujic. Mr. Cunningham and I are not appearing here on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin. We are appearing here has an accommodation to the Court. We are not here providing any legal services to Mr. Brdjanin whatsoever today and I just want to make that clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham and good morning to the three of you. So Mr. Brdjanin, I'm going to address you first. Because this is a matter which concerns - please do sit down - which concerns you personally and your rights to have -- to be represented by a lawyer of your own choice. You have just stated, Mr. Ackerman -- you've just heard Mr. Ackerman state in open court that neither he nor Mr. Cunningham are representing you as -- with immediate effect. The Trial Chamber was aware of this as from yesterday and was advised to expect a motion for adjournment of the case by Mr. Ackerman. The motion was filed yesterday late in the evening and was handed to us this morning first thing and I am going to bring the contents of this motion to your notice in case you are not aware of the entirety of its contents. Mr. Ackerman states in his motion that at around 4.00 p.m. yesterday, he was handed a request filed by a certain Mr. Hyman, who for your information is a lawyer in the Blaskic case, which he went through. Attached to that particular request of Mr. Hyman was an opinion letter from the department of the treasury of the United States of America advising Mr. Hyman that providing legal services to Mr. Blaskic without a licence would constitute a prohibited exportation of legal services in violation of section 599.201(B) of the WBSR. It is Mr. Ackerman's considered opinion that as a result of this advice, opinion letter, from the department of the treasury of the United States, both he and Mr. Cunningham in this case are currently prohibited from providing you, Mr. Brdjanin, with any legal services until they have acquired the necessary licence. Accordingly, they requested this Trial Chamber to adjourn these proceedings temporarily until the issue of licences to continue the case has been resolved. As you may well imagine, not just you but the Prosecution and Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham themselves, I together with my two colleagues took this matter with the utmost -- gave it our utmost attention for two reasons in particular, or three. Number 1, because we have a legal duty to make sure that at all times you are legally represented, and that this trial does not proceed unless you are represented as required by our statute and by our rules, and that is the first matter that we needed to address and I can assure you that we gave it our utmost attention. Second is or was that it is also our duty to ensure that if there is to be a stoppage, if there is to be a suspension of the proceedings this would last the least possible so we also addressed that matter and we have worked, if not overnight, almost overnight, in order to see what are the prospects of a possible solution in sight. The third thing is that we are definitely not contesting to Mr. Ackerman or Mr. Cunningham the evaluation of the contents of the letter that they referred to in the motion and we would certainly never dream of exposing Mr. Ackerman or Mr. Cunningham to possible Prosecution for a felony in their own country. Therefore, there is no way we are going to contest this -- to Mr. Cunningham and Mr. Ackerman. We also appreciate that they indicate in their motion that they themselves will be doing something about the situation. However, I should like to inform everyone here what we have done and what is basically appearing on the horizon, not too far off from our field of view. It seems that all this is a result of a kind of interpretation that has been given in some department in the United States by some individual which may not be in conformity with what was intended. So we may well be dealing with a mistaken interpretation of the real legal situation. Irrespective of this, the position stands. You will not have to face any proceedings being unassisted. And Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham will not be forced to represent you. The position remains as I explained to you earlier on. This matter is being worked upon, is being addressed, at the highest level at the United States, and I have been given to understand that it is in the process of being positively resolved within what I have been given to understand a very short time. And if it is positively resolved as I expect it to be positively resolved or as I have been given to understand that it will be positively resolved that would mean that Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham would be put back in a position where they can continue to represent you as they have done until yesterday. What I am saying, I'm afraid I cannot give more information on what is going on, because I would wait until I see the official documents authorising Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham to continue representing you, but the prospects are good. I have been given to understand that if there is to be a stoppage, suspension of the proceedings, this may well be for today only. Let's hope that we can reconvene tomorrow and continue with the hearing of evidence. I can assure you, Mr. Brdjanin, that if you're not represented tomorrow, there will not be a hearing. So I can assure you that we three up here will make sure that your right of representation is respected to the utmost. I don't know if you have any comments or any remarks to make in response to what I have said. If not, you may remain seated but if you're not unhappy with --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, no. I have no comments except to thank you for what you have just said and since we are in an open session, I have to say that if Mr. Ackerman leaves this case, it will be disastrous for me because I have been able to endure all this only owing to Mr. Ackerman and his team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Brdjanin. Your rights, not just this right, all your rights will be respected. You have the undertaking of this Trial Chamber. Having said that, I think we have no option but to adjourn for today. Is the witness that we were hearing yesterday present here in court or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is he in a position to be brought into the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would suggest, usher, because I understand he was not feeling well until now. Make sure with the representative of the victims and witnesses department that he is fit to be brought into the courtroom. I only need to explain to him why his presence in The Hague is no longer required for the time being and that he will need to return at some later point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are waiting, may I just on the record thank the Trial Chamber for its understanding of this very difficult situation that Mr. Cunningham and I have found ourselves in and the Trial Chamber has shown a deep understanding of that situation and appreciation for our situation and our concerns and we appreciate that a great deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman and I also want to acknowledge for the information of everyone we have had a long meeting this morning, us three judges, with the Prosecution, Ms. Korner, Ms. Sutherland, Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham, we have met for long time and I want to acknowledge publicly their high sense of responsibility and their full commitment to cooperation with the Trial Chamber in this critical moment, which hopefully will be over by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Cirkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On behalf of Judge Janu, Judge Taya and, of course, I'm also speaking for myself, also on behalf of the Tribunal in general, I should first like to apologise to you for having kept you waiting at least two hours before bringing you over to this courtroom and I am going also to explain to you, more or less, but very concisely why this happened and what's the consequence of all this. We couldn't commence the sitting at 9.00 this morning as I promised you yesterday not because of any fault on your part or any fault on any of the persons present here in this courtroom, but of circumstances that came up very unexpectedly yesterday in the afternoon. What happened was that the two lawyers, who are US citizens, who are representing Mr. Brdjanin, received a communication that a presidential order, that is an Executive Order, issued by the President of the United States sometime ago, would, according to the interpretation being given by a civil servant in the department of the treasury of the United States, prohibit them from continuing to represent Mr. Brdjanin, in this case, unless -- without a license, a proper license failing which they would be themselves exposed to criminal proceedings in the United States for a felony which is to my knowledge considered to be an extremely grievous offence. And they have asked -- they have made it clear that this being the situation, they were no longer in a position to continue representing Mr. Brdjanin until this matter is resolved. Mr. Brdjanin, who is the accused in this case, has a right to be represented by counsel of his own choosing and that being the case, it was quite obvious to us that the proceedings could not -- this trial could not proceed immediately as planned, until Mr. Brdjanin is provided with counsel of his own choosing. That is not possible to happen today. There is no way that we can provide legal assistance to Mr. Brdjanin according to the rules, which basically means that we cannot proceed today with the trial, which basically also means that what we told you yesterday, that you will come Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. forward again today to be cross-examined by Mr. Cunningham is no longer possible, which also means that you will have to come back, but you also know that you were going to be called again here to be possibly cross-examined on the draft of the book that you have finished writing and that you would like to publish. So what I thought of doing, instead of keeping you here in The Hague today, tomorrow, possibly over the weekend, hoping that this matter of legal representation will be solved and then we finish with the cross-examination that we were -- we had scheduled for today, I thought of sending you back home now and of course, you will need to come back if and when needed to be cross-examined not only on your evidence which you gave yesterday but also on the book that you have written which neither I nor Mr. Ackerman and probably neither Ms. Korner or Ms. Sutherland have had time to go through. I haven't even seen it as yet and there is no point in seeing it in the language that you have written it because I don't understand it so it needs to be translated first and then we can go through it. So what is going to happen, Mr. Cirkic, is that you are going home, and you will come back at some later point in time. I am indeed very sorry and I can assure you that everyone here is very sorry and we discussed that this morning how we could help you but there is no way that we can do anything today, so unfortunately, that's going to be the position. You will return home and then you will come back. I can assure you that I already have a team ready to give you all the assistance you need to put you at ease and enable you to return home at the earliest opportunity. Again I am very sorry. I don't know how to express myself in better terms but I also want to thank you for your cooperation, for your understanding. I'm sure I have your understanding, I'm sure you understand that this is not due to the fault of any one of us here, and that we do appreciate your patience and your cooperation. Would you like to tell us anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at first I intended to publish this book, but I'm the only one who has read this book. Nobody else has. And for a while, and I've decided not to publish this book ever, and I've been giving it a lot of thought recently and that is my -- what I've decided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is of course your decision. I mean we have no right to even intrude in that matter. I want to make sure that you understand that what has happened was beyond our control and -- in other words I want to make sure that we have your understanding by not concluding your testimony today, by sending you back, and requiring you to come back at some later point in time. Can I hear a word from you telling me yes, judge, when you need me, I will come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, right now I do not feel strong enough to go through this once again and I believe you will understand me. Yesterday, I tried to somehow summon all my strength and go through all this once again but I'm really at the end of my tether and all this is making the state of my health even worse. I do not know whether I am ready to go through what I've been through once again. Your Honours, I do not wish on anyone any time anywhere to go through a single minute of what I have experienced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I fully appreciate that, Mr. Cirkic. We'll leave it at that for the time being. I will ask the usher to accompany you, escort you out of the courtroom. Usher, please, the staff from the Victims and Witnesses Unit is waiting. Mr. Cirkic, I wish you a safe journey back home and look forward to seeing you here in this courtroom again to finish the story that you started telling us yesterday. I thank you and I wish you a safe journey.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, with Defence's permission, and with the leave the of the court -- may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no Defence at the moment, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, with leave of the court may I speak with the witness after we have adjourned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, do you have any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see no reason to object to it. Although I do not know much about these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But at this point in time, I don't think I can authorise you to speak to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think with the greatest of respect, on this occasion, Mr. Ackerman can come out of his I'm not representing Mr. Brdjanin, as an officer of the court to say he can't see the problem because he knows Ms. Sutherland. Your Honour has just heard what the witness had to say. It seems to me that unless he's spoken to by Ms. Sutherland who has been dealing with him, we are going to have severe difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland, I think you are right, Ms. Korner, but can I -- let's deal with it in a different manner. Can you limit -- tell me exactly what you want to speak to Mr. Cirkic about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's simply about the necessity, Your Honour, to reassure him about what's to happen and the necessity for him to return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that is limited only to that, I will give you my consent.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. There will be no discussion about the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to ensure that there is no discussion on the evidence. Can I also add, would you have any problems if Ms. Sutherland speaks to the witness in the presence of the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: None at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't take it as a -- any kind of distrust. It's a matter of I want to make sure that this does not come back, ricochet against us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: None at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Ms. Sutherland, you have the authorisation of the Trial Chamber and Madam Registrar, please make sure that you are present. Things being what they are we have an adjourn. We will need to live this by the hour rather than the day, Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham. I expect developments in the course of the day, developments, which can concern you directly, Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham, which could possibly make it possible for you to continue tomorrow morning. So for the time being, I'm adjourning the case until tomorrow morning. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour just kind of as an interested observer on behalf of future counsel for Mr. Brdjanin, I'm wondering if anybody is taking the responsibility for translating this book that the witness just talked about, if that's been, as to who is going to do the translation? Has that been straightened out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you, Mr. Cunningham, told us last time that you had already sent the book to the translation unit for it to be translated. I'm pretty sure that if we look at the transcript, that's how you're going to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It will probably get there today then, so that will be the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know anything about it Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, only what Mr. Cunningham represented yesterday that they were sending it to CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you want to check the transcript, you check it, but I don't think there is a need. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours, I don't know how it was interpreted. I said I did not object to the Prosecution talking to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We heard that. No, no. But we heard that but you understand, Mr. Ackerman, that when I said we need to protect your rights to the utmost, I am not just saying that for the matter -- for the sake of saying it. I say it because I mean it. And I can assure you my two colleagues mean it too. There is no way that there will be one moment in the course of this trial where you will be not protected. So we need to adjourn. We will reconvene tomorrow. You will be in the same position as today, I hope Mr. Ackerman, in the sense that if you are not reinstated by tomorrow morning, at least we would have the privilege of your presence for any assistance that the trial might need -- the Trial Chamber might need from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that and I thank you Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham. Ms. Korner is there anything else from the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So we can adjourn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 11.11 a.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of June, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
